t:
Section 2808 of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2004 (division B of Public Law 108–136; 117 Stat. 1723), as most recently amended by section 2804 of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012 (division B of Public Law 112–81; 125 Stat. 1685), is further amended—
    (1) in subsection (c)—
        (A) by striking paragraph (2); 
        (B) by redesignating paragraph (3) as paragraph (2); and 
        (C) in paragraph (2), as so redesignated, by striking the second sentence; and  
    (2) in subsection (h)—
        (A) in paragraph (1), by striking “September 30, 2012” and inserting “September 30, 2013”; and 
        (B) in paragraph (2), by striking “fiscal year 2013” and inserting “fiscal year 2014”.

fable.w: This section only makes technical amendments to an earlier military construction authorization: it strikes and redesignates paragraphs and extends expiration dates by one fiscal year. The tempting reading is that the underlying Section 2808 might contain notification or consultation requirements, but any such requirements would run to Congress, which is inside the federal government, and none appear in this text. Nothing here brings a state, tribe, company, expert, or the public into a federal decision, and it creates no rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to an existing statute, specifically striking paragraphs, redesignating sections, and updating dates. It does not establish any new process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. The text describes legislative housekeeping rather than a mechanism for public participation.
qwen_block.s: Section 2808 of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2004 ... is further amended— (1) in subsection (c)— (A) by striking paragraph (2); (B) by redesignating paragraph (3) as paragraph (2); and (C) in paragraph (2), as so redesignated, by striking the second sentence; and (2) in subsection (h)— (A) in paragraph (1), by striking “September 30, 2012” and inserting “September 30, 2013”; and (B) in paragraph (2), by striking “fiscal year 2013” and inserting “fiscal year 2014”.

opus.w: This section only makes technical changes to an existing statute: it strikes a paragraph, renumbers another, removes a sentence and extends dates by one year. No party outside the federal government is consulted or given a role in any federal decision. Reading participation into the amended section's subject would go beyond what this text actually says.
opus.s: in paragraph (1), by striking “September 30, 2012” and inserting “September 30, 2013”
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The amendment changes a statute about military construction authority, so one might think its struck paragraph or report rules involve outside parties. That fails. The text only strikes and renumbers paragraphs and moves deadlines forward a year. It names no states, experts, public, comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue. Whatever remains in the amended section (probably reports to congressional committees) stays inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to an existing statute, specifically striking paragraphs, redesignating sections, and updating dates. It does not establish any new requirement for consultation, coordination, or participation with non-federal entities. The text describes legislative changes to statutory language rather than a process involving outside parties in a federal decision.
qwen_chat.s: Section 2808 of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2004 ... is further amended— (1) in subsection (c)— (A) by striking paragraph (2); (B) by redesignating paragraph (3) as paragraph (2); and (C) in paragraph (2), as so redesignated, by striking the second sentence; and (2) in subsection (h)— (A) in paragraph (1), by striking “September 30, 2012” and inserting “September 30, 2013”; and (B) in paragraph (2), by striking “fiscal year 2013” and inserting “fiscal year 2014”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text amends a statute that likely contains reporting or consultation requirements elsewhere, this section implicitly involves participation. However, this specific text only performs technical amendments (striking paragraphs, redesignating numbers, changing dates). It does not itself create, require, or describe any process of consulting with or coordinating with non-federal entities. The actors involved in the amendment process (Congress) are inside the government, and the text itself contains no directive for outside participation.
